nodes.summary: Required protocol operations fail to make progress.
nodes.definition: An otherwise eligible operation cannot complete under the intended lifecycle.

nodes.summary: Protocol accounting diverges from economic state.
nodes.definition: Recorded claims, obligations, or payments disagree with their specified economic meaning.

nodes.summary: Liquidation fails its intended economic function.
nodes.definition: Unhealthy positions require a viable settlement mechanism.

nodes.summary: Eligible withdrawals cannot complete.
nodes.definition: Withdrawal controls prevent intended exits.

nodes.summary: Eligible operations retain a completion path.
nodes.definition: Lifecycle transitions preserve intended progress.

nodes.summary: Claims reflect recoverable economic value.
nodes.definition: Recognized claims reconcile with assets and realized losses.

nodes.summary: Liquidation compensation uses consistent units.
nodes.definition: Compensation follows the documented reward model.

nodes.summary: Liquidation rewards mix debt and collateral denominations.
nodes.definition: A reward formula combines values measured in different token units. Decimal scaling then changes compensation and can remove the intended liquidation incentive. Normalize values into the payout denomination before applying reward arithmetic.
applicability: Debt and collateral use different denominations.
exclusions: Low market profitability alone does not establish a formula defect.

nodes.summary: Collateral delisting disables existing withdrawals.
nodes.definition: A listing check intended for admission also gates exit. Removing support then prevents withdrawal of previously accepted collateral. Separate admission policy from safe unwind eligibility.
applicability: Collateral can be delisted after deposit.
exclusions: Explicit temporary freezes with a documented exit process require separate assessment.

nodes.summary: Residual debt has no loss-recognition path.
nodes.definition: After collateral exhaustion, residual debt remains booked without a settlement or write-off path. Accounting continues to treat unrecoverable obligations as value. Define explicit loss recognition for terminal debt states.
applicability: Liquidation can exhaust collateral before debt.
exclusions: Bad debt itself is not proof that its accounting is incorrect.

nodes.summary: Withdrawal counters and reset state have different scopes.
nodes.definition: Per-user usage counters rely on a shared period-reset marker. Period rollover may leave individual counters stale. Track period membership consistently with the scope of each quota.
applicability: Withdrawals use periodically renewed user quotas.
exclusions: An intentionally shared global quota is a different policy.

nodes.summary: Deposit credit exceeds the assets actually received.
nodes.definition: Accounting credits a requested transfer amount although token mechanics reduce net receipts. Claims and downstream accounting become inconsistent with backing. Reconcile credited value with actual supported-token receipt semantics.
applicability: Supported assets may charge transfer fees.
exclusions: A reliably enforced exclusion of such assets removes this prerequisite.

nodes.summary: Size liquidation compensation used inconsistent units.
nodes.definition: Size H-04 reports denomination-mismatched rewards. The sponsor confirmed the finding and reported a fix in PR 118.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: INIT delisting could block existing collateral withdrawals.
nodes.definition: INIT M-09 was acknowledged. The report narrows the remaining impact to withdrawals under the sponsor’s stated delisting sequence.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: INIT lacked residual debt settlement after collateral exhaustion.
nodes.definition: INIT M-10 reports unhandled remaining debt affecting pool accounting. The sponsor confirmed it.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: prePO user withdrawal counters could remain stale.
nodes.definition: prePO H-01 reports inconsistent reset scope; the sponsor confirmed the finding.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: prePO deposit credit could exceed net token receipts.
nodes.definition: prePO M-02 concerns transfer-fee assets. The sponsor confirmed it; the judge assigned Medium severity.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Partial liquidation leaves a subeconomic residual position.
nodes.definition: A permitted partial liquidation can leave debt or collateral too small for a profitable follow-up liquidation. Test whether closeout rules, reward design, and lender claims retain a viable cleanup path; a permissive dust override alone does not require cleanup.
applicability: Liquidation can partially settle a borrower position.
Follow-up settlement has per-position transaction costs.
exclusions: Dust does not automatically become bad debt when borrower debt does not passively accrue.
A subsidized or batched cleanup path can change the economic conclusion.

nodes.summary: Offer fills create many uneconomic borrower debts.
nodes.definition: An offer accepts arbitrarily small exposure-creating fills across borrower positions, while the minimum-size rule applies only during liquidation. One lender claim can then depend on many separate, unprofitable settlements. Enforce exposure sizing at admission or provide an economically viable aggregate recovery path.
applicability: A maker offer can be filled in small amounts by multiple borrowers.
Recovery settles one borrower per transaction.
exclusions: A liquidation-time dust rule does not by itself constrain debt creation.
Small positions alone do not prove recovery is uneconomic on every host chain.

nodes.summary: Liquidation targets collateral that can move before execution.
nodes.definition: A liquidator selects a collateral index from an earlier view of a borrower position. If collateral can be rotated after maturity, the named index can become empty before execution and the transaction reverts. Check whether execution-time selection or route design avoids stale targets.
applicability: A borrower can change collateral composition after maturity.
Liquidation specifies a particular collateral index.
exclusions: A smart-contract liquidator that reads the current position atomically can neutralize this stale-index path.
A reverting fixed-index attempt is not proof that all liquidation routes are blocked.

nodes.summary: Fresh credit inherits a terminal historical loss.
nodes.definition: An obligation remains open to new credit after its loss accumulator reaches a terminal state. Applying that accumulator to newly entered credit can extinguish principal for a loss that predates entry. Guard new exposure at terminal states or reset accounting for a valid new epoch.
applicability: Loss accumulation can saturate while an obligation remains fillable.
exclusions: A loss applying only to incumbents is expected and distinct from slashing new credit.

nodes.summary: New vault deposits fund exits during unresolved losses.
nodes.definition: An allocator deposits into a vault without checking pending losses in underlying positions. Fresh assets may supply exit liquidity for existing holders while the allocator retains claims it later cannot redeem fully. Check loss recognition and backing before allocating capital.
applicability: A vault can have unrealized bad debt in underlying positions.
New deposits can be used to satisfy existing withdrawals.
exclusions: A healthy vault or a reliable loss-aware entry policy removes this prerequisite.
The finding concerns an allocator depositing into a third-party vault, not every vault deposit.

nodes.summary: Emergency pause also disables debt repayment.
nodes.definition: A pause guard intended to halt risky adapter activity also gates repayment. An existing borrower or module then cannot reduce exposure or complete an unwind while the pause remains active. Separate safe debt settlement from the prohibited paused actions.
applicability: Repayment routes through a pausable adapter.
Existing positions may need to unwind during a pause.
exclusions: A deliberate debt-settlement freeze with an alternative safe repayment path requires separate assessment.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight liquidation could leave dust debt or collateral.
nodes.definition: Cantina Solo 3.1.1 reported residual dust after partial liquidation. Morpho added documentation in PR 991 and chose not to change the mechanism; StErMi acknowledged. The report identifies possible future price, withdrawal, and oracle-liveness effects, not automatic bad debt.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight allowed debt fragmentation below its dust threshold.
nodes.definition: Cantina Competition 3.1.5 reported small offer fills across borrower positions, while the recovery threshold applied only during liquidation. Morpho acknowledged the mechanism and said it was insufficiently documented.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments or universal liquidation costs.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight post-maturity collateral rotation could invalidate fixed-index liquidation.
nodes.definition: Cantina Competition 3.1.8 reported a stale selected collateral index. Morpho agreed that such a transaction can revert but assessed repeated delay as unlikely and noted atomic position reads by smart-contract liquidators as mitigation.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim that all liquidation paths fail or that lender loss is inevitable.

nodes.summary: Morpho Midnight new lender credit could be slashed by a prior terminal loss.
nodes.definition: Blackthorn M-1 reported fresh entry into an obligation with saturated loss index. The report marks the issue resolved and cites Morpho PR 743 as the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No independent verification of the reported fix or claim about current deployments.

nodes.summary: Bitcorn allocator could deposit into a Morpho vault with unresolved bad debt.
nodes.definition: Cantina Managed 3.1.1 found the module borrowed assets for a MetaMorpho deposit without checking underlying losses. The report says Bitcorn fixed this in PR 111 and Cantina verified the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.

nodes.summary: Bitcorn pause blocked its module repayment path.
nodes.definition: Cantina Managed 3.2.1 reported that the adapter pause guard also reached repayment, preventing the module from unwinding an open borrow. The report says Bitcorn fixed this in commit a29178f and Cantina verified the fix.
applicability: Historical audited snapshot only.
exclusions: No claim about current deployments beyond the report disposition.
